content.text:
**None of the 62 open trails here has a security score.** I fetched every open trail (`entire trail show --json`) and all of its findings (`entire trail finding --status any --freshness any --json`). Nothing in that data is a security score: no field for one, and no gate for one. The only matches for "score" were in the text of PR descriptions.

Each trail has four merge gates: `approvals`, `checks`, `findings` and `up_to_date`. The closest thing to a security signal is the agent-review findings, which have a severity and a confidence value but no security category.

**Open findings on the current code** (trails not listed have none):

| Trail | High | Med | Low |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#226 Go router group fixpoint hang](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/226) | **3** | 0 | 0 |
| [#223](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/223) | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| [#195](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/195), [#199](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/199), [#206](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/206) | 0 | 1 each | 0 |
| [#221](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/221), [#232](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/232), [#240](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/240), [#243](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/243) | 0 | 0 | 1 each |

Only #226 has open high-severity findings, which block its merge through the findings gate.

**The one security finding:** on [#250](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/250) (a dependabot pip bump), the reviewer flagged that PyJWT went to 2.15.0 when 2.15.1 fixes 13 CVEs. It was rated high and is already marked resolved.

If "security score" refers to something in the entire.io web UI, it doesn't come through the CLI. Send me a link or a screenshot and I'll check it. I can also go through #226's three high findings if that helps.

entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

Both backends act as ENTIRE_TOKEN when set, else the selected login
(--context, else $ENTIRE_CONTEXT, else the active context), so a staging
login reaches staging's control plane and cells. The cell host comes from
environment's cluster listing; an explicit ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL names the
data host directly instead.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters

## #221 [34, Δ1] feat(query): opt-in local semantic retrieval channel (draft, needs product decision)
Adds the provider's first HTTP client (opt-in semantic channel), but it is off unless two env vars are set, is restricted to loopback at URL-parse, a non-resolving custom dialer, and proxy/redirect disabling, with endpoint hashing and code-only error disclosure — a meaningful new network boundary warranting review, but no traced egress, hosted-API call, or data/credential disclosure, and no dependency/CI/subprocess changes.

## #247 [28, Δ20] fix: agent output diagnostics from #325 (subdir VERIFY, warm coverage, edges --cache-dir)
Adds a feature that reads build manifests above --repo up to the git toplevel, a genuine path-access boundary expansion, but it is contained by prefix validation rejecting ../ traversal, os.OpenRoot+Lstat symlink refusal with size caps (worktree), batch git reader IsPathSafe/validateLimitedFilePath (--head), and a subprocess preflight; all git calls are local argument-vector invocations with no-egress env guards, so no provider egress, credential exposure, or unsafe data flow is demonstrated.

## #243 [22, Δ14] perf(sem): reuse committed-tree caches across queries, worktrees and clones
Removes the absolute-path term from search/records cache keys (a deliberate loosening of cache isolation for a cache storing project-attributed symbol IDs), but replaces it with tree content-addressing, a verbatim gh/ key term, a local/ namespace ID-rebind, and a new repository-scope term, and hardens the new cross-process lock against symlink/traversal; no new network/telemetry, no dependency changes, and the only git subprocess is a pre-existing argument-vector call on local metadata.

## #240 [18, Δ4] feat(plugin): opt-in prompt-time graph context hook (Claude Code)
Minor boundary concerns in opt-in Python hook script, but all subprocess calls use safe argv-list form preventing shell injection, no shell interpolation occurs, and the provider itself is unchanged. ENTIRE_GRAPH_BIN is user-configured and equivalent to PATH modification.

## #207 [8, Δ2] bench(locate): four offline locate-cost benchmarks
Diff is limited to new local-only Python benchmark scripts under bench/locate/; all subprocess calls use argument-vector form (no shell=True/os.system/eval) with untrusted phrases passed as discrete post-`--` args to git/rg/go/the binary, and there are no network, telemetry, download, dependency, or CI changes — `git remote get-url origin` is only recorded locally, not transmitted.

## #212 [8, Δ0] fix: integrate graph correctness and accounting repairs
Clean correctness and accounting improvements with no security-relevant changes. Enhanced shell parsing is defensive classification of transcript data, not command execution. No network code, dependency changes, or egress paths introduced.

## #236 [8, Δ-5] test: compose graph launch fixes with verified replay and renderer seams
Clean maintenance release with parsing improvements, search optimizations, and development tooling. No network paths, no provider egress, no unsafe subprocess construction. Signal handling and grep alternation are bounded hardening.

## #242 [8, Δ3] fix(agentsetup): keep agents using the graph, and reach Explore/Plan subagents
Compilation error (rand.Text() doesn't exist in crypto/rand) blocks deployment but is a development bug, not a security exploit. No new network paths, telemetry, or provider-egress violations found; file write controls are properly hardened against symlink attacks.

## #248 [8, Δ0] ci: launch integration check (do not merge)
Large changeset with new hook system and file I/O, but thorough review shows proper security controls: symlink/hardlink validation, confined paths, no network operations, and maintained no-egress contract throughout.

## #251 [8, Δ4] chore(deps): bump the pip group across 1 directory with 2 updates
Routine Dependabot update of Python benchmark dependencies (multidict 6.7.1→6.9.1, urllib3 2.7.0→2.8.0) isolated to bench/memory/ harness. Zero provider code changed; no-egress contract applies only to the Go provider binary, not external benchmark tooling.

## #256 [8, Δ3] chore(deps): bump the go-minor-and-patch group with 3 updates
Clean pinned Go dependency maintenance bumping three minor versions (sys, text, scip) with no code changes and no new network capabilities; all dependencies remain used exclusively for local text processing, file system operations, and data serialization.

content.text:
I found the eval scores. Each of the 62 open trails has four eval monitors: Confidence, Drift, Risk and Security. The CLI doesn't show them, so I read them through `entire api` from `/repos/{repo_id}/trails/{n}/monitors`. That endpoint is internal and its shape could change. **Security is scored 0–100, and lower is better.**

**Overall:** none of the 62 rationales reports an exploit, credential exposure or egress path. 58 trails score 8 or below, and only four score higher than that.

| Trail | Score (change) | What the eval flagged |
|---|---|---|
| [#221 semantic retrieval channel](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/221) | **34** (+1) | It adds the provider's first HTTP client. It's off by default, allows only loopback addresses, and disables proxies and redirects.   ## Security review: trail #221, opt-in semantic channel (d0e6a627)
  
  I checked each claim by running it: a repro test in `internal/sem`, plus an end-to-end run of the built binary against a capturing server on 127.0.0.1. The review worktree has been removed. Nothing on the remote was touched.
  
  ### Claims that held up (verified)
  - **Loopback restriction** (`internal/sem/search_semantic.go:1227-1272`): every bypass form I tried was refused before any socket opened:
    - `127.1`, `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`
    - decimal `2130706433`, octal `0177.0.0.1`, hex `0x7f.0.0.1`
    - `[::127.0.0.1]` (IPv4-compatible form)
    - zone IDs `[::1%25lo0]` and `[fe80::1%25lo0]`
    - `localhost.`, `xn--localhost`, `localhost%00.evil.com`
    - `127.0.0.1%2f@evil`, and userinfo, query or fragment in the URL
  
    `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` and `LocalHost` are accepted, but both really are loopback.
  - **No DNS:** `localhost` maps straight to the literals 127.0.0.1 and ::1, and the dialer re-checks the host (`:1236-1260`). DNS rebinding is not possible.
  - **Proxy and redirects:** with `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `http_proxy` all pointed at a local listener, and the server answering 307 to a second listener, I got `http-307 proxyHits 0 otherHits 0`.
  - **Timeouts:** a body trickled out over 10s still failed at 1.00s under the context deadline.
  - **Disclosure:** errors carry only codes, the endpoint is hashed in the replay state (`:139`), and the answered model name is compared but never echoed.
  - **Activation:** only the two environment variables turn it on (`internal/cli/env.go:38-39`, `:118-122`). No repo config file is read.
  - **Tests:** every test URL is loopback, or a non-loopback form that the tests expect to be refused (`8.8.8.8`, `192.0.2.1`, `embed.example.com`).
  - **What a server's answers can steer:** nominated files must be in the corpus (`:335-355`) and are rendered through the normal source read path. A hostile server can reorder in-repo results but cannot inject text.
  
  ### Findings, by severity
  1. **Medium: `--no-network` is silently ignored and the channel still sends source text. VERIFIED.**
     - `index.go:325` and `search.go:2831` accept `--no-network` and do nothing with it, and `provider.go:1825` discards `NoNetwork`.
     - I ran `index --no-network --semantic` and then `query --head --no-network` with the two variables set. My listener received:
       - `{"input":["search_document: rotate. SECRET_DOC_COMMENT internal key rotation func Rotate(k string) string"]}`
       - `{"input":["search_query: rotate keys"]}`
     - So a caller or wrapper that relies on the explicit flag for a no-egress guarantee gets HTTP traffic carrying doc comments (up to 40 lines), signatures and the query.
  2. **Medium (documentation and contract): the no-egress claims are now false when the channel is on, and the PR doesn't update them.**
     - `README.md:16,36` and `AGENTS.md:18` still say "no network requests, model calls". `AGENTS.md:228` forbids hosted API calls; this channel is a model call over HTTP, even if it's loopback-only.
     - `docs/search.md` gets a section, but it never acknowledges the exception.
  3. **Low–Medium: a squatter on the loopback port receives repo text. PLAUSIBLE (by design).**
     - Nothing authenticates the daemon, and it's plain HTTP.
     - On a shared or multi-user host, or with any other local process, whoever binds 127.0.0.1:11434 first gets every eligible function's name, doc comment and signature during the index build, plus every later query string.
     - It can also return crafted vectors to promote chosen in-corpus files to the top of results. If the repo already contains prompt-injection text, this amplifies it.
  4. **Low: a local server can exhaust memory during the build. PLAUSIBLE, not executed.**
     - The build path reads up to 256 MiB per batch (`:79`) into memory and then decodes it with `json.Unmarshal` into `[][]float64`.
     - A body of `0,0,0,…` decodes to about 8 bytes per 2 input bytes, plus slice growth, so roughly 1–2 GB of memory. This is a crash risk, not egress.
  5. **Low: repo-supplied activation through an agent harness. PLAUSIBLE.**
     - The provider reads no repo config, but a cloned repo's `.claude/settings.json` `env` block or a mise `[env]` section (once trusted) could set both variables.
     - The loopback check caps the damage, so this is only a route into finding 3.
  
  ### Score
  34/100 is about right, perhaps a little high for the network mechanics themselves. The transport hardening held against every bypass I tried. The real risk is the contract gap, not a network escape: `--no-network` is quietly overridden, and README and AGENTS still promise no network or model calls. Fixing finding 1 (make `--no-network` force the channel off, or reject it with `--semantic`) and finding 2 (document the exception) would justify roughly 20–25. Findings 3 and 4 are residual risks of the opt-in design.
</agent-message>

    - `localhost.`, `xn--localhost`, `localhost%00.evil.com`

  - **Proxy and redirects:** with `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `http_proxy` all pointed at a local listener, and the server answering 307 to a second listener, I got `http-307 proxyHits 0 otherHits 0`.
  - **Timeouts:** a body trickled out over 10s still failed at 1.00s under the context deadline.
  - **Disclosure:** errors carry only codes, the endpoint is hashed in the replay state (`:139`), and the answered model name is compared but never echoed.
  - **Activation:** only the two environment variables turn it on (`internal/cli/env.go:38-39`, `:118-122`). No repo config file is read.
  - **Tests:** every test URL is loopback, or a non-loopback form that the tests expect to be refused (`8.8.8.8`, `192.0.2.1`, `embed.example.com`).
  - **What a server's answers can steer:** nominated files must be in the corpus (`:335-355`) and are rendered through the normal source read path. A hostile server can reorder in-repo results but cannot inject text.

  1. **Medium: `--no-network` is silently ignored and the channel still sends source text. VERIFIED.**
     - `index.go:325` and `search.go:2831` accept `--no-network` and do nothing with it, and `provider.go:1825` discards `NoNetwork`.
     - I ran `index --no-network --semantic` and then `query --head --no-network` with the two variables set. My listener received:
       - `{"input":["search_document: rotate. SECRET_DOC_COMMENT internal key rotation func Rotate(k string) string"]}`
       - `{"input":["search_query: rotate keys"]}`
     - So a caller or wrapper that relies on the explicit flag for a no-egress guarantee gets HTTP traffic carrying doc comments (up to 40 lines), signatures and the query.
  2. **Medium (documentation and contract): the no-egress claims are now false when the channel is on, and the PR doesn't update them.**
     - `README.md:16,36` and `AGENTS.md:18` still say "no network requests, model calls". `AGENTS.md:228` forbids hosted API calls; this channel is a model call over HTTP, even if it's loopback-only.
     - `docs/search.md` gets a section, but it never acknowledges the exception.
  3. **Low–Medium: a squatter on the loopback port receives repo text. PLAUSIBLE (by design).**
     - Nothing authenticates the daemon, and it's plain HTTP.
     - On a shared or multi-user host, or with any other local process, whoever binds 127.0.0.1:11434 first gets every eligible function's name, doc comment and signature during the index build, plus every later query string.

     - The build path reads up to 256 MiB per batch (`:79`) into memory and then decodes it with `json.Unmarshal` into `[][]float64`.
     - A body of `0,0,0,…` decodes to about 8 bytes per 2 input bytes, plus slice growth, so roughly 1–2 GB of memory. This is a crash risk, not egress.
  5. **Low: repo-supplied activation through an agent harness. PLAUSIBLE.**
     - The provider reads no repo config, but a cloned repo's `.claude/settings.json` `env` block or a mise `[env]` section (once trusted) could set both variables.
     - The loopback check caps the damage, so this is only a route into finding 3.

The real risk is the contract gap, not a network escape: `--no-network` is quietly overridden, and README and AGENTS still promise no network or model calls. Fixing finding 1 (make `--no-network` force the channel off, or reject it with `--semantic`) and finding 2 (document the exception) would justify roughly 20–25. Findings 3 and 4 are residual risks of the opt-in design.

The #221 review is back (score 34). I confirmed its main finding in the source: on the branch, `--no-network` is a no-op flag at `index.go:325` and `search.go:2831`, and `provider.go:1825` discards it (`_ = options.NoNetwork`).

**The network hardening held.** The reviewer ran every check against a capturing listener on 127.0.0.1:
- **Loopback bypasses:** tried `127.1`, `0.0.0.0`, decimal, octal and hex IPs, IPv4-compatible IPv6, zone IDs, `localhost.` and URL-userinfo tricks. All were refused before any socket opened.
- **DNS, proxies, redirects:** the client never does DNS lookups, so DNS rebinding is impossible. Proxy environment variables are ignored and redirects aren't followed.
- **Other claims:** the 1s timeout holds and errors show only codes.
- **Activation:** the channel turns on only through the two environment variables.
- **Server influence:** a hostile local server can reorder results within the repo but cannot inject text.

**Findings:**
1. **Medium, verified: `--no-network` is silently ignored.** With the channel on, `index --no-network --semantic` and `query --no-network` still sent doc comments, signatures and the query text over HTTP. A wrapper that relies on that flag for a no-egress guarantee is wrong.
2. **Medium: the docs still promise no network or model calls.** `README.md:16,36` and `AGENTS.md:18` say so, and `AGENTS.md:228` forbids hosted API calls. The PR doesn't mention this exception.
3. **Low–Medium, plausible: anything listening on the port gets repo text.** There is no authentication and the traffic is plain HTTP. Whatever binds 127.0.0.1:11434 first receives function names, doc comments, signatures and queries, and can rerank results.
4. **Low, plausible: a local server can exhaust memory.** A response up to 256 MiB is decoded into `[][]float64`, which could use roughly 1–2 GB.
5. **Low, plausible: a cloned repo could switch it on.** A repo's `.claude/settings.json` `env` block or mise `[env]` could set both variables. The loopback restriction caps the damage. This is just a mention of the file, not an instruction to change any settings.

**Verdict:** 34 is about right. The risk is the gap between what the flags and docs promise and what the code does, not an escape to the network. Fixing findings 1 and 2 would justify a score around 20–25.

**Still running:** #247, #243 and #240.

But it missed what is new here. This hook turns attacker-controllable repo text into model context automatically, under a header that sounds like the tool, and without the guaranteed untrusted framing the project's own forgery rules (`search_forgery.go`, agent-guide) aim for. content.text:
The #247 review is back (score 28). There's no injection and no egress, and the reviewer judged the score about right.

**Findings:**
1. **Low/Medium, verified: repo config can move the VERIFY command outside the checkout.** A repo's `core.worktree = ../..` setting redefines where "the git toplevel" is. The new VERIFY line then becomes `cd ../../.. && go test …` and lands outside the checkout, for example in `~/Downloads`.
   - This needs a repo whose `.git` directory arrives in an archive; a normal clone can't carry that setting.
   - Fix: refuse to walk above `--repo` when `core.worktree` is set, or when the toplevel isn't the directory that contains `.git`.
2. **Low, verified: a symlinked `--repo` sends `cd` to the wrong place.** `cd ../..` moves through the logical (symlinked) path, while the manifest was read from the physical toplevel. So the command runs in a tree the analysis never looked at. Fix: emit an absolute `cd`, or use `cd -P`.
3. **Info: a race between two file checks.** Between the symlink check and the open, someone with write access could swap in a FIFO, which would make the read hang. That's a denial-of-service risk only.

**Held up under testing:** no manifest content reaches the command except through quoting or allowlists. FIFOs, `/dev/zero` and oversized manifests are refused. `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` are stripped from git's environment. `edges --cache-dir` writes nowhere new.

The reviewers shared scratch space, and one had a binary deleted mid-run, so it rebuilt in a private subdirectory. The #247 results weren't affected. I'll check that this didn't affect #243, which is still running.

Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  ## Security review of trail #243, `perf/cache-reuse-across-worktrees` @ 2f4adfda
  
  I found one real regression, which I reproduced. The others are low severity or already existed before this branch. Nothing was pushed or posted. Both scratch worktrees (`wt243` and a base worktree, `wtbase`, that I added to compare against) are removed.
  
  ### 1. LOW-MEDIUM — History-derived relations leak between clones that share a tree (VERIFIED, new in this branch)
  
  **Where:** `internal/sem/search_cache.go:1149-1215` (key), `:859-883` (loader). The relation is built at `provider.go:1542` / `:12810`.
  
  **Cause:** The search key is the tree hash, a scope term, and `gh/<owner>/<repo>` taken from the origin URL as-is. It no longer includes the checkout path. But `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` comes from **commit history** (`gitutil.FileCochanges(repo, revision)`), not from the tree. The loader only restamps `Commit` and `RepoRoot`, so the edges from whichever clone built the entry first are served to every other clone.
  
  **Exploit:** An attacker repo sets origin to `https://github.com/victim/repo.git`, matches the victim's final tree, and uses its own made-up history. The victim clones it locally next to the real checkout, which shares the default per-user cache.
  
  **Repro:** two repos, same tree `5a4ceaa…`, opposite co-change histories, shared `--cache-dir`:
  - Victim on a private cache: `b.go … 4 recent commits`, `c.go … 2`.
  - After the attacker clone warms the shared cache, `impact --repo victim --head --symbol Alpha` reports `b.go … 2`, `c.go … 4`. That is the attacker's history.
  - The base binary (`origin/fix/close-p1-highs`), same steps: the victim keeps its own `4/2`. So this is a regression.
  
  **Limits:** the attacker can only choose pairs and counts among files that really exist in the tree. Symbol content, IDs, snippets and VERIFY lines are tree-bound and cannot be poisoned, because tree equality means content equality.
  
  **Non-adversarial version of the same bug:** shallow clones, or worktrees on different branches that reach the same tree, get each other's co-change data.
  
  **Fix:** hash the commit, or a history digest, into the key whenever the profile emits `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`; or strip the edges and recompute them on load.
  
  ### 2. LOW — A held build lock stalls cold queries for 60s (VERIFIED)
  
  **Where:** `cache_build_lock.go:15` and `:68-104`, used at `search_cache.go:503` and `:540`.
  
  **Repro:** I held flock on the `.build.lock` from python, then ran a cold `query --head`. It took 80.4s against 16.9s unheld. The query does not hang: it gives up after 60s and builds without the lock.
  
  **Who can do it:** the same user, or anyone with write access to a shared `--cache-dir`. A stopped (Ctrl-Z) or background agent holding the lock causes the same 60s delay.
  
  Lock files are never deleted, by design, so empty files pile up one per key.
  
  ### 3. INFO — Lock-file symlink and TOCTOU handling holds up (VERIFIED)
  
  I planted a symlink to an outside file at the lock name. The query succeeded (rc=0, running unlocked), the target was unchanged, and nothing was created through the link. The lock open uses Lstat before, an `os.Root` confined walk, `O_EXCL` on create, and `SameFile` after. A planted symlink does silently turn locking off, which is harmless.
  
  ### 4. INFO — Not regressions
  
  - **Path traversal:** none. Cache filenames are validated sha256 hex (`cache_entry.go:52`); remote-URL text only goes through the hash.
  - **Permissions:** directories are 0700 and files 0600 (checked with stat).
  - **Shared cache dirs:** an existing shared dir is not re-chmodded, and entries are field-validated but not integrity-protected. That was equally true on base, where the path in the key was guessable anyway.
  - **Ignore inputs:** `.graphignore`, ignore/include flags and their contents, the resolved max-files cap, the built-in secret rules, and the scope are all in the key.
  - **Worktree data:** cannot leak in. The key function refuses `Worktree`, and the loader also checks the worktree flag on load.
  - **Restamping:**
    - The records-cache rewrite (`records_cache.go:271-290`) needs exactly one unescaped `"repo_root":` in line 1. Repo content cannot forge that, because quotes inside JSON strings are escaped.
    - The `local/` ID rebind (`search_cache.go:901`) only rewrites the key prefix. It is sound given the tree is the content address.
  
  ### Verdict on 22/100
  
  **About right, perhaps slightly high.** The eval's main worry, impersonating `gh/victim/repo` to poison symbols, snippets or VERIFY lines, does not work: tree content-addressing blocks it. What does get through is narrower: history-derived co-change hints, only after the victim clones an attacker repo with an identical tree on the same machine. That rates low to medium for integrity and is mostly a correctness bug. The lock is well hardened, and its DoS is bounded at 60s.
  
  I'd put it at 15–20, with finding 1 as the one item to fix before merge.
</agent-message>

  ## Security review of trail #243, `perf/cache-reuse-across-worktrees` @ 2f4adfda
  
  I found one real regression, which I reproduced. The others are low severity or already existed before this branch. Nothing was pushed or posted. Both scratch worktrees (`wt243` and a base worktree, `wtbase`, that I added to compare against) are removed.
  
  ### 1. LOW-MEDIUM — History-derived relations leak between clones that share a tree (VERIFIED, new in this branch)
  
  **Where:** `internal/sem/search_cache.go:1149-1215` (key), `:859-883` (loader). The relation is built at `provider.go:1542` / `:12810`.
  
  **Cause:** The search key is the tree hash, a scope term, and `gh/<owner>/<repo>` taken from the origin URL as-is. It no longer includes the checkout path. But `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` comes from **commit history** (`gitutil.FileCochanges(repo, revision)`), not from the tree. The loader only restamps `Commit` and `RepoRoot`, so the edges from whichever clone built the entry first are served to every other clone.
  
  **Exploit:** An attacker repo sets origin to `https://github.com/victim/repo.git`, matches the victim's final tree, and uses its own made-up history. The victim clones it locally next to the real checkout, which shares the default per-user cache.
  
  **Repro:** two repos, same tree `5a4ceaa…`, opposite co-change histories, shared `--cache-dir`:
  - Victim on a private cache: `b.go … 4 recent commits`, `c.go … 2`.
  - After the attacker clone warms the shared cache, `impact --repo victim --head --symbol Alpha` reports `b.go … 2`, `c.go … 4`. That is the attacker's history.
  - The base binary (`origin/fix/close-p1-highs`), same steps: the victim keeps its own `4/2`. So this is a regression.
  
  **Limits:** the attacker can only choose pairs and counts among files that really exist in the tree. Symbol content, IDs, snippets and VERIFY lines are tree-bound and cannot be poisoned, because tree equality means content equality.
  
  **Non-adversarial version of the same bug:** shallow clones, or worktrees on different branches that reach the same tree, get each other's co-change data.
  
  **Fix:** hash the commit, or a history digest, into the key whenever the profile emits `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`; or strip the edges and recompute them on load.
  
  ### 2. LOW — A held build lock stalls cold queries for 60s (VERIFIED)
  
  **Where:** `cache_build_lock.go:15` and `:68-104`, used at `search_cache.go:503` and `:540`.
  
  **Repro:** I held flock on the `.build.lock` from python, then ran a cold `query --head`. It took 80.4s against 16.9s unheld. The query does not hang: it gives up after 60s and builds without the lock.
  
  **Who can do it:** the same user, or anyone with write access to a shared `--cache-dir`. A stopped (Ctrl-Z) or background agent holding the lock causes the same 60s delay.
  
  Lock files are never deleted, by design, so empty files pile up one per key.
  
  ### 3. INFO — Lock-file symlink and TOCTOU handling holds up (VERIFIED)
  
  I planted a symlink to an outside file at the lock name. The query succeeded (rc=0, running unlocked), the target was unchanged, and nothing was created through the link. The lock open uses Lstat before, an `os.Root` confined walk, `O_EXCL` on create, and `SameFile` after. A planted symlink does silently turn locking off, which is harmless.
  
  ### 4. INFO — Not regressions
  
  - **Path traversal:** none. Cache filenames are validated sha256 hex (`cache_entry.go:52`); remote-URL text only goes through the hash.
  - **Permissions:** directories are 0700 and files 0600 (checked with stat).
  - **Shared cache dirs:** an existing shared dir is not re-chmodded, and entries are field-validated but not integrity-protected. That was equally true on base, where the path in the key was guessable anyway.
  - **Ignore inputs:** `.graphignore`, ignore/include flags and their contents, the resolved max-files cap, the built-in secret rules, and the scope are all in the key.
  - **Worktree data:** cannot leak in. The key function refuses `Worktree`, and the loader also checks the worktree flag on load.
  - **Restamping:**
    - The records-cache rewrite (`records_cache.go:271-290`) needs exactly one unescaped `"repo_root":` in line 1. Repo content cannot forge that, because quotes inside JSON strings are escaped.
    - The `local/` ID rebind (`search_cache.go:901`) only rewrites the key prefix. It is sound given the tree is the content address.
  
  ### Verdict on 22/100
  
  **About right, perhaps slightly high.** The eval's main worry, impersonating `gh/victim/repo` to poison symbols, snippets or VERIFY lines, does not work: tree content-addressing blocks it. What does get through is narrower: history-derived co-change hints, only after the victim clones an attacker repo with an identical tree on the same machine. That rates low to medium for integrity and is mostly a correctness bug. The lock is well hardened, and its DoS is bounded at 60s.
  
  I'd put it at 15–20, with finding 1 as the one item to fix before merge.

| [#247 agent diagnostics](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/247) | 28 | About right | VERIFY's `cd ../..` can land outside the inspected checkout, through a repo-local `core.worktree` or a symlinked `--repo`. Emit an absolute `cd` and refuse the walk upward when `core.worktree` is set. |
| [#243 cache reuse](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/243) | 22 | A bit high (15–20) | **Regression, verified against the base branch:** the cache key is now the tree only, but co-change data (which files change together) comes from commit history. So clones that share a tree get each other's history. Add the commit or a history digest to the key. |
| [#240 prompt hook](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/240) | 18 | **Too low (~30)** | Repo text is injected on every prompt under a heading that sounds like the tool itself, with no guaranteed untrusted label; the heading can be forged at column 0. On Windows, `shutil.which` may run an `entire.exe` from the repo. |
| [#251 pip bump](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/251) | 8 | About right | Nothing. Every hash matches PyPI and there are no advisories. One caveat: after merge, the lockfile is installed in a nightly job that can mint cloud credentials (`id-token: write`) and needs no reviewer approval. |

**Fix first:**
1. **#243**: history leaking between clones. It's a real regression and the fix is small.
2. **#221**: make `--no-network` actually force the channel off and document the exception. This directly contradicts the project's no-egress rule.
3. **#240**: wrap the hook output in a fixed untrusted-data frame. Of the five, this is the one where the eval undersold the risk.

**Smaller items:**
- **#247:** a race between the symlink check and the file open could make the manifest read hang; it needs write access to the checkout.
- **#243:** a held build lock stalls a cold query for up to 60s.
- **#240:** a timed-out hook leaves a child process running, and the first 160 characters of the prompt are visible in `ps`.
- **#221:** whatever squats on 127.0.0.1:11434 receives repo text, and a local server can exhaust memory with a huge response.
- **PyJWT:** still pinned at 2.15.0. OSV lists no advisories for it, so the CVE claim from the #250 review is unconfirmed.

The reviewers used temporary copies of each branch, and those are removed. I confirmed the #221, #240 and #243 headline findings in the branch source myself; the reproductions are the reviewers'. Nothing was posted to any trail. I can add these as trail findings if you want, or write them up as a page.

1	name: locomo-nightly
     2	
     3	# Nightly full LoCoMo (n=1540) for the entire-graph arm only.
     4	#
     5	# SECURITY MODEL — why an external contributor cannot trigger this, and why there
     6	# is no long-lived credential in this repository:
     7	#
     8	#   * `schedule` fires ONLY on the default branch of THIS repository. A fork
     9	#     cannot schedule a workflow in the upstream repo, so the nightly path is
    10	#     unreachable from outside.
    11	#   * `pull_request_target` is deliberately ABSENT. It is the one trigger that
    12	#     hands repository secrets to code from a fork, and it is the standard
    13	#     exfiltration route. Do not add it to this file.
    14	#   * `workflow_dispatch` already requires write access and uses the reviewer-
    15	#     protected `benchmark` environment. Scheduled runs use the separate
    16	#     `benchmark-nightly` environment: main-only, but without required reviewers,
    17	#     so a human gate cannot silently turn the nightly into a queued manual run.
    18	#   * `if: github.repository == ...` stops the job even if this file is copied
    19	#     into a fork that has its own schedule enabled.
    20	#   * There is NO stored Azure API key. During the benchmark step the harness
    21	#     obtains a short-lived GitHub OIDC assertion and exchanges it directly for a
    22	#     short-lived Foundry data-plane bearer token. The token provider refreshes
    23	#     both credentials as needed during the multi-hour run. Deleting the federated
    24	#     credential or its resource-scoped role assignment revokes access.
    25	#
    26	#   Honest limit: `id-token: write` is job-wide, so code in any step can request a
    27	#   GitHub OIDC assertion. CI installs the complete Python graph from exact wheel
    28	#   hashes with dependency discovery disabled, and exposes the Entra identifiers
    29	#   only to the benchmark step. Those controls prevent package drift; approved
    30	#   runtime code still executes with identity access and must itself be trusted.
    31	#
    32	# One-time setup this workflow depends on is documented in
    33	# bench/memory/RUNNING-LOCOMO.md ("Nightly CI").
    34	
    35	on:
    36	  schedule:
    37	    # 06:00 UTC daily. The run takes ~2.5-3.5h, so it lands well before the
    38	    # working day in either US or EU.
    39	    - cron: "0 6 * * *"
    40	  workflow_dispatch:
    41	    inputs:
    42	      reason:
    43	        description: "Why this manual run (recorded in the run summary)"
    44	        required: false
    45	        default: "manual"
    46	
    47	# Default deny. Each job re-grants only what it needs.
    48	permissions: {}
    49	
    50	# One benchmark at a time. A second run would contend for the same Foundry
    51	# deployment quota and both would record throughput-shaped drops that look like
    52	# arm weakness rather than contention.
    53	concurrency:
    54	  group: locomo-nightly
    55	  cancel-in-progress: false
    56	
    57	jobs:
    58	  locomo:
    59	    # Never run in a fork, even if this file is copied there with a schedule.
    60	    if: github.repository == 'entireio/entire-graph'
    61	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    62	    # Last-resort ceiling for setup + benchmark + diagnostics. The benchmark
    63	    # command has its own earlier graceful deadline so always() steps still get
    64	    # time to summarize and upload completed per-question records.
    65	    timeout-minutes: 330
    66	    # Both environments are restricted to main and are separate immutable,
    67	    # repository-ID-bound OIDC subjects.
    68	    # `benchmark` has required reviewers; `benchmark-nightly` deliberately does
    69	    # not. The Entra app trusts only these two exact subjects and has only MaaS
    70	    # data-plane actions on the one Foundry resource (see the documented custom
    71	    # role; the broader built-in Cognitive Services User role is not used).
    72	    environment:
    73	      name: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'benchmark-nightly' || 'benchmark' }}
    74	    permissions:
    75	      contents: read
    76	      id-token: write # OIDC token for Azure federation. Nothing else.
    77	
    78	    steps:
    79	      - name: Check out entire-graph
    80	        uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
    81	        with:
    82	          persist-credentials: false
    83	
    84	      - name: Set up Go
    85	        uses: actions/setup-go@d35c59abb061a4a6fb18e82ac0862c26744d6ab5 # v5.5.0
    86	        with:
    87	          go-version: "1.27.x"
    88	
    89	      - name: Build entire-graph and put it on PATH
    90	        run: |
    91	          set -euo pipefail
    92	          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
    93	          go build -o "$HOME/bin/entire-graph" ./cmd/entire-graph
    94	          echo "$HOME/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
    95	          "$HOME/bin/entire-graph" version || true
    96	
    97	      - name: Set up Python
    98	        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
    99	        with:
   100	          python-version: "3.12"
   101	
   102	      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
   103	      # Harness. The upstream benchmark is Apache-2.0 third-party code and is NOT
   104	      # vendored here (see bench/memory/UPSTREAM.md); it is reconstructed from a
   105	      # pinned commit plus this repo's patches, preserving the audited benchmark
   106	      # configuration with the documented keyless-authentication successor.
   107	      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
   108	      - name: Reconstruct the pinned upstream harness
   109	        env:
   110	          UPSTREAM_COMMIT: 4b61c5d31b9c668a12b4f5e78064248a02c82d2b
   111	        run: |
   112	          set -euo pipefail
   113	          git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/mem0ai/memory-benchmarks.git "$HOME/mem0harness"
   114	          cd "$HOME/mem0harness"
   115	          git checkout --quiet "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT"
   116	
   117	          # Content pin. UPSTREAM.md fixes this file's md5 at the pinned commit;
   118	          # if it does not match, the clone is not what the published numbers ran
   119	          # against and the run must not proceed.
   120	          expected=abdbb9f272e4265153b7e3e71837007e
   121	          actual=$(md5sum benchmarks/common/metrics.py | cut -d' ' -f1)
   122	          if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
   123	            echo "::error::upstream metrics.py md5 $actual != pinned $expected"
   124	            exit 1
   125	          fi
   126	
   127	          for p in "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/patches/000[1-4]-*.patch \
   128	                   "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/patches/0006-*.patch; do
   129	            git apply -p1 "$p"
   130	          done
   131	          cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/benchmarks/common/*.py benchmarks/common/
   132	          cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/requirements-lock-py312.txt .
   133	
   134	          python -m venv .venv
   135	          .venv/bin/python -m pip install \
   136	            --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --no-deps \
   137	            -r requirements-lock-py312.txt
   138	          .venv/bin/python -m pip check
   139	
   140	      - name: Fetch the LoCoMo dataset
   141	        run: |
   142	          set -euo pipefail
   143	          cd "$HOME/mem0harness"
   144	          mkdir -p datasets/locomo
   145	          curl -fsSL -o datasets/locomo/locomo10.json \
   146	            https://raw.githubusercontent.com/snap-research/locomo/main/data/locomo10.json
   147	          # The audited dataset copy. LOCOMO-COMPARISON.md 6b pins this hash; a
   148	          # different corpus is a different benchmark, so fail rather than score it.
   149	          expected=79fa87e90f04081343b8c8debecb80a9a6842b76a7aa537dc9fdf651ea698ff4
   150	          actual=$(sha256sum datasets/locomo/locomo10.json | cut -d' ' -f1)
   151	          if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
   152	            echo "::error::locomo10.json sha256 $actual != pinned $expected"
   153	            exit 1
   154	          fi
   155	
   156	      - name: Run LoCoMo (entire-graph arm, n=1540)
   157	        id: benchmark
   158	        # Backstop around the command-level graceful timeout below. This remains
   159	        # below the job ceiling so later always() steps can still run.
   160	        timeout-minutes: 285
   161	        # Keep this as the first step that receives the Entra identifiers:
   162	        # checkout, reconstruction, and dependency installation complete first.
   163	        # `id-token: write` itself is job-wide; see the security note above.
   164	        env:
   165	          # These are identifiers, not credentials, and are deliberately scoped
   166	          # to this step. With `id-token: write`, GitHub also injects the
   167	          # ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_* values used by the refreshable assertion
   168	          # callback. The harness exchanges each assertion directly with Entra;

**CI failures:** all three were on Windows, and they look like a lost runner, not a problem with the PR.

- "Coverage and integrity" and the overall Windows check failed only because shard 2's evidence was missing.
- #251 changes only a Python lockfile under `bench/memory`, which the Go tests don't use, and main's last eight test runs all passed.

The rerun is in progress. I'll tell you the result when it finishes; Windows shards can take up to about 45 minutes.

**My finding:** I suggested moving the lockfile install out of the nightly job that can mint cloud credentials (`id-token: write`). That wouldn't reduce any risk.
- The install uses `--only-binary=:all:`, and installing a wheel runs no package code.
- The packages only execute later, inside the benchmark step. That step needs `id-token: write` to exchange tokens with Azure over the multi-hour run.
- `locomo-nightly.yml:26-30` already documents this as a known limit.

I dismissed the finding on [#251](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/251) with that explanation, so #251 has no open findings now.

content.text:
The eval is right that CI never installs or tests these packages. I checked them locally instead, and **#251's dependencies work: 111 harness tests pass and every harness module loads with them.**

I reproduced the nightly's setup in a scratchpad:
- **Setup matches the nightly:** I rebuilt the upstream harness at its pinned commit, confirmed its checksum, and applied this repo's patches. Then I installed the #251 lockfile with the nightly's flags (`--require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --no-deps`).
- **Install:** all hashes verified, `pip check` is clean, and urllib3 2.8.0 and multidict 6.9.1 load.
- **Imports:** all 22 harness modules import. Between them they load both changed packages, via requests→urllib3 and aiohttp/yarl→multidict.
- **Tests:** 74 harness tests pass, including `test_entra_auth`, plus 37 from the bench-memory kit. Four are skipped by design because they only run in the kit checkout.

One correction: the Entra token exchange uses httpx, not urllib3. The earlier review's guess that urllib3 carries the OIDC traffic was wrong, so urllib3 runs alongside the credential rather than handling it.

**Limits:** this ran on macOS arm64, while the nightly runs on Linux. It also didn't make a real model call, because that needs the Azure OIDC identity.

**CI rerun:** every Windows job except shard 2 has passed, and shard 2 is still running. That fits the earlier runner-loss explanation. I'll report when it finishes.

To close the gap for good, I could add a PR-triggered CI job that runs exactly this check whenever `bench/memory/` changes. It would need only read access and no OIDC identity, and it would cover this and every future Dependabot bump. That's a separate PR against main, so should I open it? I can also post this verification as a comment on [#251](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/251).

name: bench-memory-kit

# Reproducibility guards for the LoCoMo reproduction kit under bench/memory:
# adapter configuration must be portable or required-and-validated, a failed
# retrieval subprocess must not be scored as an empty retrieval, the launcher
# must refuse a resume mode it cannot honour, and the patch set that CI applies
# to the freshly cloned upstream harness must be internally consistent.
#
# Pure standard-library Python: the adapters under test import nothing external,
# so this job needs no dependency installation and cannot drift with the lock.

on:

  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7.0.0
        with:

name: bench-memory-guards

on:

  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:

1	# AGENTS.md — operating guide for coding agents
2	
3	Hand this to any coding agent working in a repo where the `entire graph` plugin
4	is installed. It moves initial code-location work from broad grep/read
5	exploration to targeted graph queries. Token impact depends on the task and the
6	model, so treat any single figure as scenario-dependent; the measured range and
7	the conditions behind it are in the [README](README.md).
8	
9	Two guidance surfaces coexist here on purpose. `.entire/agent-guide.md` is the
10	generated activation artifact — regenerated in full by `init-agents`, so never
11	edit it by hand — and is what agents load through the managed block at the end
12	of this file. This document is the maintained long-form reference; its examples
13	pass flags explicitly (such as `--format text`) for readability rather than
14	relying on command defaults.
15	
...

159	
160	**When:** a human asks what the graph is buying them. Agents should not run it as part of a coding task.
161	
162	---
163	
164	## Repository-specific workflow
165	
166	Follow `.entire/agent-guide.md`, generated from repository state. Both Graph-only
167	and combined instructions make the same first-action obligation: the first action on
168	any task that requires finding code is ONE
169	`entire graph query --repo . --profile full --query "<task>"`.
170	That holds for small edits, follow-ups, tasks that already name the file, and tasks
171	where a Brain brief has already reported locations — a brief reports where code is,
172	not what depends on it. Combined instructions also begin substantive orientation with
173	`entire brain brief "<task>" --json` unless equivalent task context is available.
174	Use Graph for discovery, structural analysis, and semantic revision comparisons, and
175	Brain for retained knowledge, prior decisions, and checkpoint/session history.
176	
177	Current source and executed tests establish present behavior; historical answers
178	explain prior intent. Investigate disagreements. A failed query is reported and falls
179	back to direct source inspection for that query only — it does not retire the tool for
180	the session — and does not authorize automatic installation, configuration, or repair.
181	See [the contract](docs/agent-coordination.md).
182	
183	## Operating doctrine
184	
185	1. **Answer the information gap.** Follow the generated workflow; query Graph when further discovery is needed.
186	2. **Treat results as evidence, not truth.** Read focused source around the result and widen the check when behavior, aliases, generated code, or dynamic dispatch could matter.
187	3. **Use graph follow-ups when they answer a real question.** `impact`, `callers`, and `neighbors` are appropriate for blast radius and related-site checks; avoid exploratory whole-graph dumps.
188	4. **Make the smallest complete change.** Check sibling sites and contracts when the task implies them.
189	5. **Verify before stopping.** Run the `VERIFY:` command when query prints one; it may be a whole-suite fallback when no narrow command exists. Never report that tests pass without having run them. If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and disclose the limitation.
...
206	If your task is modifying this repository (not just using it), the build/test surface is in `mise.toml`:
207	
208	```sh
209	mise run build   # go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph  (needs CGO for tree-sitter)
210	mise run test    # go test ./...
211	mise run check   # fmt + vet + race tests + build
212	```
213	
214	Contract rules that must not break: schema `1.x` is frozen and additive-only (`docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`); the provider is **no-egress** (never add remote fetches, hosted API calls, telemetry, or runtime grammar downloads); `compound-v1` symbol IDs must stay stable across ordinary edits, and any parser change that RE-KEYS existing symbols must bump `IdentityRevision` (`internal/sem/provider.go`) in the same commit — the record and search caches are keyed on the git tree of the source, which a parser edit does not change, so without the bump upgraded users keep being served the old symbols from a stale cache and the fix is invisible; unsupported/unparseable files must surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops. All logic lives under `internal/` (`sem` = parsing/graph/search, `cli` = hand-rolled dispatch, `gitutil` = git subprocess); `cmd/entire-graph/main.go` is a thin entry point. The plugin manifest (`entire-plugin.yml`) registers the subcommand `graph`, so users type `entire graph ...`. This project was **previously named `entire-sem`** — do not reintroduce the old name. **Entire Brain** (`entire-brain`) is the separate downstream consumer of this provider's NDJSON — not an old name for this project.
215	
216	### Working in a scratch worktree: adopt the session first
217	
218	Entire binds an agent session to the worktree it started in, and links a commit to
219	that session through a `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer added by its git hooks. Commits
220	made in a DIFFERENT worktree are not linked: no checkpoint, no trailer, and the
221	work is absent from `entire checkpoint list` even though the hooks are healthy and
222	`entire doctor` reports nothing wrong.

content.content:
entire graph adds a deterministic, no-egress code graph to Entire checkpoints.

Usage:
  entire graph <command> [flags]

Set up your agent:
  init-agents      Install the coding-agent guide into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
  agent-guide      Print the coding-agent operating guide
  index            Build/warm a committed-tree cache variant for matching queries
  capabilities     List parsed languages, relation types, and features

Inspect the graph:
  search           Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)
  neighbors        Who calls this / what does it call (targeted relations)
  impact           One-shot blast radius for changing a symbol
  def              What a name IS: declaration, fields, and method surface
  explain          Resolve symbols named by a failing build or test
  symbols          Stream every symbol definition (bulk NDJSON)
  edges            Stream every relation (bulk NDJSON)
  snapshot         Stream the whole graph: files, symbols, and relations (bulk NDJSON)
  snapshot-query   Query a compact snapshot without rebuilding the graph

Analyze changes & more:
  commit           Entity-level change list for a commit vs its first parent
  diff             Entity-level change list between two refs
  checkpoint       Analyze the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
  verify           Run a test command and return an adjudicated verdict, not test output
  stats            Human report: graph usage vs grep/read, and estimated token savings

Help & diagnostics:
v0.4.0

# The locked third-party dependencies of the LoCoMo harness are otherwise first
# exercised by the nightly, after merge, in a job that holds `id-token: write`.
# The kit and guard jobs are stdlib-only on purpose, so a bump of
# requirements-lock-py312.txt (Dependabot or manual) would land without any CI
# ever installing or importing it. This job closes that gap on the PR: it
# reconstructs the harness exactly as locomo-nightly.yml does, installs the lock
# with the nightly's flags, imports every harness module, and runs the harness's
# offline unit tests against the locked versions.
#
# It makes no model calls and consumes no tokens: no `id-token`, no secrets, no
# Azure variables. The only network access is the pinned upstream clone and the
# hash-pinned wheel downloads.
name: bench-memory-deps

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "bench/memory/**"
      - ".github/workflows/bench-memory-deps.yml"
      - ".github/workflows/locomo-nightly.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "bench/memory/**"
      - ".github/workflows/bench-memory-deps.yml"
      - ".github/workflows/locomo-nightly.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  bench-memory-deps:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # Keep in step with "Reconstruct the pinned upstream harness" in
      # locomo-nightly.yml: same commit, content pin, patch set, and install flags.
      - name: Reconstruct the pinned upstream harness
        env:
          UPSTREAM_COMMIT: 4b61c5d31b9c668a12b4f5e78064248a02c82d2b
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/mem0ai/memory-benchmarks.git "$RUNNER_TEMP/mem0harness"
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/mem0harness"
          git checkout --quiet "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT"

          expected=abdbb9f272e4265153b7e3e71837007e
          actual=$(md5sum benchmarks/common/metrics.py | cut -d' ' -f1)
          if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
            echo "::error::upstream metrics.py md5 $actual != pinned $expected"
            exit 1
          fi

          for p in "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/patches/000[1-4]-*.patch \
                   "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/patches/0006-*.patch; do
            git apply -p1 "$p"
          done
          cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/benchmarks/common/*.py benchmarks/common/
          cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/bench/memory/requirements-lock-py312.txt .

          python -B -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -B -m pip install \
            --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --no-deps \
            -r requirements-lock-py312.txt
          .venv/bin/python -B -m pip check

      - name: Import every harness module against the locked dependencies
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/mem0harness
        run: |
          .venv/bin/python -B - <<'PY'
          import importlib
          import pkgutil

          import benchmarks

          failed = []
          count = 0
          for module in pkgutil.walk_packages(benchmarks.__path__, "benchmarks."):
              if ".test_" in module.name:
                  continue
              try:
                  importlib.import_module(module.name)
                  count += 1
              except Exception as exc:  # report every broken module, not just the first
                  failed.append(f"{module.name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
          print(f"imported {count} harness modules")
          for line in failed:
              print(f"::error::{line}")
          if failed or count == 0:
              raise SystemExit(1)
          PY

      - name: Harness unit tests (reconstructed layout)
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/mem0harness
        run: >-
          .venv/bin/python -B -m unittest -v
          benchmarks.common.test_entra_auth
          benchmarks.common.test_runmeta

      - name: Kit unit tests (repository layout) on the locked interpreter
        run: >-
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/mem0harness/.venv/bin/python" -B -m unittest -v
          bench.memory.benchmarks.common.test_bm25_client
          bench.memory.benchmarks.common.test_kit_reproducibility

## Why

The LoCoMo harness's third-party lock (`bench/memory/requirements-lock-py312.txt`) is first exercised by `locomo-nightly`, **after merge**, in a job that holds `id-token: write`. `bench-memory-kit` and `bench-memory-guards` are stdlib-only on purpose, so a Dependabot bump such as #251 lands with no CI ever installing or importing it. The trail's confidence eval flagged exactly this.

## What

A new `bench-memory-deps` workflow. It runs only when `bench/memory/**`, itself, or `locomo-nightly.yml` changes, and it:

1. Reconstructs the pinned upstream harness the same way the nightly does: same commit, `metrics.py` md5 pin, patches 0001–0004 and 0006, and copied adapters.
2. Installs the lock with the nightly's flags (`--require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --no-deps`), then runs `pip check`.
3. Imports every non-test harness module and reports every failure.
4. Runs `test_entra_auth` and `test_runmeta` in the reconstructed layout, then `test_bm25_client` and `test_kit_reproducibility` in the repository layout, all on the locked interpreter.

## Token and credential use

None. The job has `permissions: contents: read` only, with no `id-token`, secrets, or Azure variables, and makes no model calls. `test_entra_auth` uses mocked transports and `.test` hosts. The only network access is the pinned upstream clone and the hash-pinned wheel downloads.

## Verification

- `actionlint` 1.7.12 passes (shellcheck was not installed locally).
- I ran every `run:` step locally (macOS arm64, Python 3.12) against main's lock: 22 modules imported, 74 harness tests OK (4 skipped by design outside the kit checkout), and 37 kit tests OK.
- The same checks against #251's lock (urllib3 2.8.0, multidict 6.9.1) also pass.

The reconstruction block is duplicated from `locomo-nightly.yml`, with a comment asking that the two stay in step. Extracting it into a shared script would mean editing the OIDC-holding nightly job, which I left out of scope.

EOF

content.text:
I added a CI job that installs and tests the bench dependencies on every relevant PR, and it already passes in CI. #251's CI is green again. #251 can't merge yet because of a merge conflict and a missing approval.

**New CI job:** [PR #339](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/339), trail [#257](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/257).
- `bench-memory-deps` runs when anything under `bench/memory/` or either related workflow changes. It rebuilds the pinned harness exactly as the nightly does and installs the lockfile with the nightly's flags. It then imports every harness module and runs the harness and kit unit tests.
- **No tokens:** it has read-only permissions, no OIDC identity, no secrets and no Azure variables. The Entra tests use mocked transports with fake `.test` hosts, so nothing is called for real.
- **Verified:** I ran every step locally against main's lockfile and they all passed, and actionlint is clean. On the PR, `bench-memory-deps` passed in 26 seconds.
- **To keep in sync:** the rebuild step is copied from `locomo-nightly.yml`, with a comment asking that the two stay in step. Sharing one script would mean editing the nightly job that holds the OIDC identity, so I left that out.

**#251:**
- **CI:** the rerun passed, including shard 2, which confirms the earlier failure was a lost runner.
- **Comment:** I posted the local verification as a discussion on the trail, linking PR #339.
- **Gates:** checks and findings now pass. "Approvals" still needs a reviewer.
- **Merge conflict:** the "up_to_date" gate now fails on a conflict with main, most likely the lockfile MD5 line in `FAIR-CONFIG.md`. Commenting `@dependabot rebase` on the GitHub PR should regenerate it, but I haven't done that. Should I?
